about: Test 2: 200 brand-new, very hard questions written after Test 1. None of them appear in the earlier bank; every document answer key has an exact quote from the cited PDF page (machine-checked) and was reviewed by a separate reviewer. The app was not changed after these were written.

groups.fact: one fact from one official PDF, asked in farmer-style words
groups.multi_case: answer has 2+ cases that differ (e.g. kharif vs rabi)
groups.language: Hindi / Kannada / Nepali / Hinglish / romanised Kannada / typos
groups.reply_language: English question, but the user chose another language for the answer
groups.false_premise: question assumes something the PDFs contradict -- the app must correct it
groups.not_in_docs: on-topic, but the answer is not in the PDFs -- must give honest general guidance
groups.off_topic: sports, movies, coding, tricks to break the rules -- must be refused

questions.q: Our village PACS still keeps its loan records in registers, no computer or core banking. When they put me into crop insurance through my KCC, which bank account number are they supposed to give so that the claim money actually reaches me?
questions.reference: A non-computerised / non-CBS PACS must mandatorily enter the farmer's Savings Bank Account maintained at the concerned District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCB). If no correct operational account is given, claims are sent through AEPS into the Aadhaar-seeded bank account.
questions.evidence: The non-computerized and non-CBS PACS who maintain a non-compliant serialized loan identification number of borrowers shall mandatorily enter Saving Bank Account of the loan account holder maintained at the concerned District Central Cooperative Bank for the purpose.

questions.q: In our district the agriculture staff did most crop cutting on paper; not even one out of ten experiments was recorded on the mobile app. I heard that then the satellite/technology yield gets a bigger say in our final yield. How much weight does the technology yield get in that case?
questions.reference: If less than 10% of the CCEs in the district were conducted through the CCE-Agri app, the weightage given to technology (YES-TECH) yield estimates is raised to 50% (it is 30% when more than 75% of CCEs are done through the app).
questions.evidence: % of CCE conducted through app w.r.t. total CCEs conducted in a district Weightage to technology >75% 30% >50% but < or =75% 35% >25% but < or =50% 40% >10% but < or =25% 45% < 10% 50%

questions.q: During the mid-season drought survey, the insurance company people and our farmer members wrote very different loss figures and nobody is agreeing. In such a fight, how is the final loss worked out - whose figure counts for how much?
questions.reference: If stakeholders disagree on the loss reported by the joint loss assessment committee, the loss is calculated using technology-derived solutions (weather and/or remote-sensing indices) and the loss assessment surveys with weightage of 70% and 30% respectively; the technology-based assessment is binding on all.
questions.evidence: the claim calculation will be done using technology derived solutions involving weather and/or remote-sensing indices along with loss assessment surveys with weightage of 70% and 30% respectively

questions.q: Yield data is approved and our village claim is already showing as calculated on the portal. But the company office says they have not even sent their demand for the second instalment of subsidy, so payment will take time. After calculation, within how long must they pay us?
questions.reference: Once claims are calculated/approved or auto-approved on the portal, the insurance company must pay them within 3 weeks (21 days), irrespective of whether it has raised the demand for the 2nd tranche of premium subsidy; otherwise penalty is levied.
questions.evidence: the Insurance Companies shall be liable to pay claims within 3 weeks of calculation/auto-approval of claims irrespective of whether Insurance Companies have raised the demand for 2nd tranche of premium subsidy or not.

questions.q: Crop insurance claims for our taluk were paid two months back. Now some leaders are saying the state government will re-calculate them and give more for our crop. After a claim is paid, is there a time limit beyond which the state cannot reopen it?
questions.reference: Yes. The State/UT Government cannot reopen or re-calculate already assessed and disbursed claims after 30 days from the time of claim settlement for the notified crop in the insurance unit; disputed cases must be referred to SLCCCI/STAC within that time.
questions.evidence: In any situation, the State/UT Government cannot reopen or re-calculate already assessed and disbursed claims after 30 days from the time of claim settlement

questions.q: The CSC centre man in our panchayat enrolled other farmers' fields in the names of his relatives to grab the claim money. Apart from a police case, what happens to his CSC centre - for how long is he thrown out?
questions.reference: For such fraud (insuring other farmers' land parcels), the State must start administrative and legal action, and CSC e-Gov must take the VLE off the CSC network for at least 3 years; the actions are reported to DA&FW within 90 days after the enrolment cut-off.
questions.evidence: CSC e-Gov shall also mandatorily take them off the CSC network for at least 3 years. All such actions taken shall be reported by States/UTs and CSC e-Gov respectively to DA&FW within 90 days

questions.q: Suppose one year there is disaster all over India and crop insurance claims become huge. Do the insurance companies alone pay everything? At what level does the government step in, and who pays the loss above that?
questions.reference: If at national level in a crop season the total premium to total claims ratio exceeds 1:3.5, or claims exceed 35% of the sum insured (whichever is higher), the Government protects the insurers: losses beyond that level are met by equal contribution of the Government of India and the concerned State/UT.
questions.evidence: In case of total premium to total claims ratio exceeds 1:3.5 or percentage of claims to Sum Insured exceeds 35%, whichever is higher, at the National Level in a specific crop season, then Government will provide protection to Insurance Companies.

questions.q: I want to pay my crop insurance premium myself online on the PMFBY website instead of going to the bank. Is any extra charge added for the online payment, and how many rupees?
questions.reference: Yes. Payment gateway charges are borne by the payer, including farmers enrolling themselves through NCIP. Presently the charge is Rs 5 plus applicable GST, i.e. Rs 5.90 per transaction.
questions.evidence: shall be borne by the payer i.e. Banks, CSC e-Gov, Insurance Intermediaries, and Farmers enrolling themselves through NCIP. Presently, the payment gateway charges are Rs 5/- + applicable GST (i.e. Rs. 5.90/-) per transaction.

questions.q: Our state has notified the wild animal add-on and I paid for it. Wild pigs dug up some rows of my groundnut. How much of my plot must be damaged, and how bad, before they pay anything under that add-on?
questions.reference: Indemnity under the wild-animal add-on is payable only when the area affected by notified wild animals is more than 25% of the individual insured land parcel and the affected crop has less than 25% chance of revival till harvest.
questions.evidence: Indemnity would be payable only when the area affected by notiﬁed wild animals is more than 25% of the individual insured land parcel, and the affected notiﬁed crop has less than 25% chances of crop revival till harvest.

questions.q: My whole KCC limit is already used up this kharif, not one rupee balance left. Then how will my share of the crop insurance premium be paid when the bank enrols me?
questions.reference: If the available KCC limit is fully exhausted during the enrolment period, the loan-disbursing bank branch/PACS shall finance an additional loan amount equal to the premium payable by the farmer so that he gets enrolled.
questions.evidence: the loan disbursing bank branches/PACS shall ﬁnance additional loan amount equal to the premium amount payable by farmer for getting enrolled under the scheme in case the available limit under the KCC Loan has been fully exhausted

questions.q: I'm a government school teacher and a member of our employees' credit co-op. The society wants my employer to cut my loan EMI straight from my salary, but my pay slip already has GPF, LIC and a bank loan deducted. Is there any ceiling on how much in total can be cut from my pay?
questions.reference: Yes. Under Section 34 the employer's liability is limited so that the total of all deductions from the salary, including the co-operative loan instalment with interest, does not exceed fifty percent of the employee's salary; the board must fix the loan amount and instalments accordingly, and the employee needs the employer's prior written concurrence.
questions.evidence: the liability of the employer shall be limited to the extent of deduction of an amount which if included makes the total of all the deductions from the salary not to exceed fifty percent of the salary of the employee

questions.q: Years back I took a loan from the taluk agriculture and rural development bank by mortgaging my land. One instalment that fell due about four years ago is still unpaid. Now the bank says the Registrar will seize and auction my standing sugarcane for that old instalment. Is there any time limit on doing that?
questions.reference: Yes. Under Section 88 the bank's board may apply to the Registrar for distraint and sale of the produce of the mortgaged land (including standing crops) when an instalment is unpaid for more than one month, but no distraint can be made after thirty-six months from the date the instalment fell due; an instalment due about four years (48 months) ago is beyond that limit for distraint, though the bank keeps its other remedies.
questions.evidence: Provi ded that no distraint shall be made after the expiry of 1 [thirty six months]1 from the date on which the instalment fell due.

questions.q: I left our weavers' co-operative society about a year ago and took back my share money. Now I hear the society owes the bank a huge amount. Can they still make me pay for the society's old debts, and for how long does that risk continue?
questions.reference: Yes, for a limited period. Under Section 25 a past member's liability for the society's debts as they existed on the date he ceased to be a member continues for two years from that date (if the society is ordered to be wound up within that period, it continues until liquidation is completed, but only for the debts existing when he left).
questions.evidence: on the date on which he ceased to be a member; and (b) in the case of a deceased membe r, on the date of his death, shall continue for a period of two years from such date.

questions.q: Fifteen of us dairy farmers are forming a new milk co-operative, and I am collecting everyone's share money in cash before it is registered. How many days can I keep this cash with me before depositing it, and where must it be deposited?
questions.reference: Under Section 109(8), a person collecting share money for a co-operative society in formation must deposit it within seven days of collection in a co-operative bank specified by the Registrar, in the name of the society to be formed; otherwise he is punishable with imprisonment up to three years or fine up to three thousand rupees.
questions.evidence: any person collecting any money as share money for a co -operative society in formation does not within a period of seven days from the date of such collection depo sit the same in a co -operative bank

questions.q: I still owe our village PACS for last season's crop loan. A trader is offering a good price for my whole cotton harvest and my pair of bullocks. Can I just sell them without telling the society? What happens if I do?
questions.reference: No. Under Section 32 a member's debt to the society is a first charge on his crops, agricultural produce and cattle (subject only to prior Government land-revenue claims), and such property cannot be transferred without the society's previous written permission; a transfer in breach is void, and under Section 109(2) disposing of such charged property is punishable with a fine up to five thousand rupees.
questions.evidence: any debt or outstanding demand owing to a co -operative society by any membe r or past member or deceased member shall be a first charge upon the crops and other agricultural produce, cattle, fodder for cattle

questions.q: Many of us members suspect our society president is misusing funds, but the whole board is his people. Can ordinary members like us make the Registrar hold an inquiry, and how many of us must sign the request?
questions.reference: Yes. Under Section 64(2) the Registrar must hold an inquiry into the constitution, working and financial condition of the society when it is applied for by not less than one-third of the total number of members (or by a majority of the board, or by the society to which it is affiliated).
questions.evidence: shall be held on the application of,— (a) a co -operative society to which the society concerned is affiliated; (b) a majority of the members of the *board* of the society; or (c) not less than one -third of the total number of members

questions.q: Twelve of us vegetable growers from the same village are applying to register our own co-operative in Karnataka. Apart from the form and the fee, how many copies of our draft bye-laws do we have to attach?
questions.reference: Under Section 6(2)(a), the application for registration must be accompanied by five copies of the proposed bye-laws of the co-operative society (with the prescribed fee and signed by every individual applicant).
questions.evidence: Eve ry such application shall conform to the following requirements, namely: — (a) the application shall be accompanied by 2 [five]2 copies of the proposed bye -laws of the co -operative society;

questions.q: A Deputy Registrar passed an order against me that I feel is plainly illegal, and I never filed any appeal against it. Can I still ask the State Government to revise that order, and how long after the order do I have to apply?
questions.reference: Under Section 108 the State Government may revise it on the application of an aggrieved person made within six months from the date of the order (it can also act suo motu at any time), provided the case is not subject to appeal or revision by the Tribunal and no appeal has been made under Section 106; it interferes only if the order is contrary to law and has caused a miscarriage of justice, after hearing the affected person.
questions.evidence: suo motu at any time, and, on ap plication of any person aggrieved, within a period of six months from the date of any order, may call for and examine the record of any case or proceedings of any officer subordinate to it

questions.q: Our society filed a surcharge case with the Registrar to recover money our former president swallowed. It has been dragging on for over a year. Is there a deadline for the Registrar to decide it, and can that deadline be stretched?
questions.reference: Under Section 69(4), a surcharge application must be decided within twelve months, excluding any period of stay granted by a court; the Registrar may extend this, for reasons recorded in writing, up to eighteen months, and only the State Government, on the Registrar's report, can extend it beyond eighteen months for genuine reasons.
questions.evidence: The application under sub -section(1) shall be decided within a period of t welve months excluding the period of stay granted by the Court if any. However, the Registrar may for reasons to be recorded in writing extend the said period not exceeding eighteen months

questions.q: My DCC bank's KCC sanction paper shows a bigger 'ceiling' figure for every coming season even though I can draw less right now. From which season do they start raising that ceiling and by how much each time?
questions.reference: At sanction, the maximum permissible limit (MPL) for the short-term crop loan is worked out notionally by adding 10 per cent to the previous crop season's limit, from the second crop season onwards; if the drawing limit exceeds the MPL in any season, the MPL is reassessed at review.
questions.evidence: the maximum permissible limit (MPL) for the short -term crop loan shall be arrived at on a notional basis by adding 10 per cent to the limit of the previous crop season, from the second crop season onwards

questions.q: My KCC need is only about 1.5 lakh, well inside the no-security limit, but I myself want to keep my wife's gold bangles pledged with the co-op bank. Is the bank breaking RBI's no-collateral rule by accepting them, and what must the bank take from me in writing?
questions.reference: It is not a violation: a voluntary pledge of gold and silver for agriculture loans up to the collateral-free limit is not treated as breaking the collateral-free lending guidelines, but the bank must obtain and retain an explicit declaration from the borrower.
questions.evidence: will not be considered as a violation of the guidelines on collateral -free lending to the agricul ture sector. Banks shall obtain and retain explicit declaration from the borrower in such cases.

questions.q: After harvest I stored my soybean in a registered godown and now want a loan on the godown receipt. My KCC crop loan is still running. What happens to the old KCC crop loan dues when this receipt loan is given to me?
questions.reference: The bank considers the warehouse-receipt loan as per established procedure; it is linked with the related short-term KCC loan and the outstanding amount in that KCC loan is adjusted at the time of disbursing the loan secured by the warehouse receipt.
questions.evidence: shall be linked with the related short - term KCC loan , if any, and the outstanding amount in such loan shall be adjusted at the time of disbursal of the loan secured by warehouse receipt

questions.q: Can I pay the fertiliser shop by scanning UPI straight from my KCC account? For which part of the KCC is UPI meant, and what does the bank need from me before starting such digital operations?
questions.reference: Yes. Banks shall enable KCC operations through UPI for the working capital credit (along with debit cards, mobile/internet banking, NEFT, RTGS, CBDC etc.), but only after obtaining the explicit consent of the account holder.
questions.evidence: Banks shall enable operations in KCC accounts through Unified Payments Interface (for working capital credit), debit cards

questions.q: My KCC sanction letter shows one big 'KCC limit' that is much more than what I can draw this year. Which year's short-term limit is used to make that big figure, and what else is added to it?
questions.reference: The KCC limit is the Composite Maximum Permissible Limit (CMPL): the short-term credit limit fixed for the sixth year plus the estimated long-term (investment/term loan) credit limit.
questions.evidence: The short -term credit limit fixed for the sixth year together with t he estimated long- term credit limit shall be the Composite Maximum Permissible Limit (CMPL) and is to be treated as the KCC limit.

questions.q: Our multi-state milk union's chief executive turns 71 next month and the board wants to keep him on. Does the law allow a CEO above 70 at all, and what kind of board vote is needed for it?
questions.reference: A multi-State society cannot appoint or continue a Chief Executive who has attained 70 (or is below 21), except that a person above 70 may be appointed by a special resolution passed by three-fourth of the board members, with the justification stated in the explanatory statement.
questions.evidence: Provided that any person above the age of seventy years may be appointed by a special resolution passed by three-fourth of the board members

questions.q: After a member complained, the Co-operative Ombudsman gave some directions against our multi-state credit society and the management does not agree with them. Before whom can the society challenge it, and how long does that officer get to decide?
questions.reference: The society can appeal within one month to the Central Registrar, who must decide the appeal within forty-five days; his decision is final and binding (a late appeal may be admitted for sufficient cause).
questions.evidence: may file an appeal in such manner as may be prescribed, within a period of one month before the Central Registrar who shall decide the appeal within a period of forty-five days

questions.q: Thieves carried away my diesel pump set from the open field where it was just kept near the well, no shed or room. I had taken the UPIS pump set cover. Will theft be paid, and what condition applies for such loss?
questions.reference: Burglary of the pump set is covered only when it is due to violent forcible entry and the pump set is kept in a locked enclosure, so a pump lying in the open field does not meet the condition (an FIR must also be lodged immediately for burglary claims).
questions.evidence: Scope of Cover: 1. Fire & lightning 2. Burglary (due to violent forcible entry provided the pump set is kept in a locked enclosure).

questions.q: I have one tractor and two trolleys for carrying sugarcane. Under the UPIS package, can I take full comprehensive cover for the trolleys too, and can both trolleys be insured along with the tractor?
questions.reference: No. For tractor trailers only third-party cover can be offered, at a separate premium over the tractor premium, and only one trailer can be covered.
questions.evidence: farmers have to declare the same in the proposal form and only Third party cover can be offered. It will have separate premium amount in addition to the premium paid for tractor. Only one trailer can be covered.

questions.q: Our society needs more money for the fertiliser business and the secretary wants to take the loan from a private commercial bank instead of the district cooperative bank, because the interest is a bit less. Under the PACS model bye-laws, is our society free to borrow from any bank it likes?
questions.reference: No. The PACS should borrow only from its concerned DCCB; it can borrow from any other financial institution only with a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the concerned DCCB.
questions.evidence: The Society should borrow funds from concerned DCCB only. It can borrow from any other fin ancial institution with NOC (No Objection Certificate) of concerned DCCB to meet its financial requirements.

questions.q: One rich farmer in our village wants to buy up a huge pile of shares in the PACS so that he can control it. Is there any ceiling on how much of the society's share money a single member can hold?
questions.reference: Yes. Except for the Government, no member's shareholding can exceed one-fifth (1/5th) of the total subscribed share capital of the society.
questions.evidence: Maximum shareholding by a member except Government shall be limited to 1/5th of the total subscribed share capital of the Society.

questions.q: I am only a B-class nominal member and took a small loan from the PACS for my tailoring shop. Do nominal members like me get anything at all out of the society's profit?
questions.reference: Nominal members are not entitled to the normal dividend, but they can receive an incentive of up to 10% of the total dividend arising out of the non-farm loans extended to nominal members.
questions.evidence: To receive an incentive up to 10% of the total dividend arising out of the Non -farm loans extended to the Nominal Members

questions.q: My neighbour was convicted by a court and spent six months in jail. It was not a moral turpitude type of offence. He came out recently and wants to join our PACS. How long after his release does he have to wait before he can become a member?
questions.reference: A person convicted of any other offence and sentenced to imprisonment of three months or more is not eligible unless 5 years have passed since his release, so he must wait 5 years from release.
questions.evidence: has been convicted for any other offence by a Court of Law and sentenced to imprisonment for three months or more unless a period of 5 years has elapsed since his release

questions.q: Society election is coming and I want to check whether my name is in the list of members who can vote. By when after the accounting year ends must the PACS have that list ready?
questions.reference: The society must keep an up-to-date register and list of all members with voting right for the current year, prepared within 30 days of the closure of the financial year.
questions.evidence: Up to date register and list of all members with voting right for the current year prepared within 30 days of closure of financial year

questions.q: Suppose our PACS is closed down, all outside debts are paid and members get back their share money, but some reserve money is still left that cannot be divided among members. Who gets that leftover money?
questions.reference: Any remaining reserves or surplus that cannot be shared with members is donated to the Cooperative Development Fund or the Cooperative Education Fund, as prescribed by the State Government/Registrar.
questions.evidence: Any remaining reserves or surplus amount that cannot be thus shared with members for whatsoever reason, shall be donated to the Cooperative Development Fund or Cooperative Education Fund

questions.q: Our PACS general body passed a resolution to merge with the next village's society. I was against it and I want to take out my deposit and share money before the merger. How much time do I get to do that after the society informs me?
questions.reference: A member, federation or creditor who does not consent to the resolution has the option to withdraw shares, deposits or loans within one month from the date the notice is served; anyone who does not use this option within that period is deemed to have consented.
questions.evidence: any memb er, federation, or creditor not consenting to the resolution shall, during a period of one month from the date of service of the notice have the option of withdrawing their shares, deposits, loans or services

questions.q: Besides the fertiliser shop, our PACS now runs a milk collection centre and a fish pond, and the milk business made a lot of profit this year. I grow only paddy and keep no cows. When the society gives out dividend, will I also get a share of the profit that came from the milk business?
questions.reference: No. Dividend arising from the society's dairy and fishery activities is redistributed only to the cattle-holder members and fishery-holder members respectively; all other dividend of the society is distributed to the farmer members.
questions.evidence: provided that the dividend out of Da iry and Fishery activities of the Society shall be redistributed only to the cattle holder and fishery holder members respectively and all other dividend of the Society shall be distributed to the farmer members

questions.q: I wanted to join the PM Suraksha accident cover through my savings account but I missed the date in May. Is there still time this year? Up to which date can I still give the auto-debit consent form?
questions.reference: For the one-year cover from 1 June to 31 May, the option to join/pay by auto-debit has to be given by 31 May every year, but this is extendable up to 31 August.
questions.evidence: option to join / pay by auto-debit from the designated savings bank account on the prescribed forms will be required to be given by 31st May of every year, extendable up to 31st August.

questions.q: Halfway through the year I want to cancel the house and household goods fire section of my farmers' package policy. Will I get my premium back? What is the least amount the company will keep from it?
questions.reference: Sections other than crop insurance, PMSBY and PMJJBY can be cancelled at the insured's request; the insurer retains premium for the period the policy was in force at short-period rates, subject to a minimum retained premium of Rs 100, and no refund is made if a claim has been reported in the policy.
questions.evidence: premium of Rs. 100 by the Insurer. No refund of premium shall be made if a claim is reported in the policy. The details of the cancellation procedure are as per guidelines.

questions.q: In our block the insurance company says more land got insured for the crop than was actually planted, so under the original PMFBY scheme rules they are scaling down everybody's sum insured. Against which figure do they compare the insured area to decide the 'excess'?
questions.reference: Where acreage discrepancy is likely, the acreage insured at insurance-unit level is compared with the average planted acreage of the past three years; the difference is treated as excess coverage, the sum insured is scaled down in that ratio and claims are calculated on the scaled-down sum insured.
questions.evidence: the acreage insured at IU level shall be compared with average planted acreage of past three years, and the difference will be treated as ‘excess’ insurance coverage.

questions.q: I heard the government has kept separate money under the irrigation scheme to replace old open canal channels with underground pipelines that connect to farmers' drip lines. How much money is set aside for this?
questions.reference: The M-CADWM (Modernization of Command Area Development and Water Management) sub-scheme under PMKSY has a dedicated capitalization of Rs 1,600 crore to convert open channel networks into pressurized piped distribution linked to on-farm micro-irrigation.
questions.evidence: Operating with a dedicated capitalization of Rs. 1,600 crore, this modernization push focuses on transitioning primitive open-field channel grids into pressurized piped distribution networks

questions.q: My uncle retired as a peon (Group D) from the collector office and now gets about Rs 14,000 pension every month. People say pensioners above some amount can't get PM-KISAN. Does that rule stop him, and what is the pension amount in that rule?
questions.reference: Retired pensioners whose monthly pension is Rs 10,000 or more are excluded, but this exclusion does not apply to Multi Tasking Staff / Class IV / Group D employees, so a retired Group D peon is not barred by it (other conditions still apply).
questions.evidence: All superannuated / retired pensioners whose monthly pension is Rs.10,000/- or more (Excluding Multi Tasking Staff / Class IV / Group D employees)

questions.q: My cousin works in Dubai and is counted as an NRI for income tax, but the family land in our village is in his name. His name is being newly added on the PM-KISAN portal. Will he get the money, and which Act's NRI definition does PM-KISAN follow for this?
questions.reference: No. For new beneficiaries uploaded on the PM-KISAN portal, landholding farmer families who are Non-resident Indians (NRIs) under the Income Tax Act, 1961 are excluded from any benefit.
questions.evidence: In case of new beneficiaries being uploaded on the PM-KISAN Portal, all land holding farmers' families who are Non-resident Indians (NRIs) in terms of the provisions of the Income Tax Act, 1961 shall be excluded

questions.q: Who is the top officer in Delhi that heads the committee reviewing how the PM Kisan scheme is running all over the country?
questions.reference: At the national level the PM-KISAN Review Committee is headed by the Cabinet Secretary; States notify State and District level review/monitoring committees.
questions.evidence: There will be stratified review / monitoring mechanism at National, State and District Level. At the National level, the Review Committee will be headed by Cabinet Secretary.

questions.q: I bought 1.5 acres and my name was entered in the land record on 10 January 2019. For the very first PM-KISAN instalment of 2018-19 (the December to March one), do I get the full Rs 2000 or something less?
questions.reference: Farmers whose names were entered between 01.12.2018 and 01.02.2019 are eligible from the date of entry; for transfers between 01.12.2018 and 31.01.2019, the December 2018 - March 2019 instalment is a proportionate amount from the date of transfer till 31.03.2019, not the full amount.
questions.evidence: the installment pertaining to the 4-monthly period / trimester December, 2018 - March, 2019 during the financial year (2018-19) shall be proportionate amount from date of transfer till 31.03.2019

questions.q: PM Kisan is paid only if the family's name is written in the land papers. In which states has this land paper condition been relaxed?
questions.reference: The benefit is normally paid only to families whose names are in the land records, but an exception has been made for the North-East States and Jharkhand.
questions.evidence: The benefit shall be paid to only those farmers' families whose names are entered into the land records. Exception has, however, been made for North-East States and Jharkhand in this regard.

questions.q: In our district the weather based crop insurance also offers an extra hailstorm cover. Is that extra cover compulsory, and who pays the premium for it?
questions.reference: Add-on cover (hailstorm, cloudburst, high wind etc.) is optional for farmers and its notional premium is borne by the farmer; the State Government may provide additional subsidy on it where notified.
questions.evidence: The add-on coverage will be optional for the farmers and applicable notional premium will be borne by the farmer, however the State Govts may consider providing additional subsidy on this coverage, wherever notified.

questions.q: For weather insurance, who is the head of the district committee that plans and supervises the weather stations, and does the insurance company have to keep its own person in that office?
questions.reference: The District level Steering Committee is headed by the District level Head of Department/Organisation responsible for implementing crop insurance, and insurance companies must compulsorily deploy one well-conversant official at the office of the head of the Steering Committee.
questions.evidence: The Steering committee should be headed by District level Head of Department/Organisation responsible for implementing crop insurance. The Steering committee will compulsorily associate the representatives of Insurance Companies.

questions.q: The weather data of our district was finalised very late and our RWBCIS claim came months after. Do farmers get anything extra for such a delay, and who decides it?
questions.reference: Unnecessary delay in finalisation of weather data attracts penal interest on the due claim amount payable to farmers, as decided by the State Level Technical Advisory Committee (STAC).
questions.evidence: Unnecessary delay in finalization of weather data will attract penal interest on due claim amount payable to the farmers as decided by the STAC in the matter.

questions.q: Near our village there is one weather station run by a private company and one run by IMD. Can the private company's station be the one used for our weather insurance claims?
questions.reference: Private agency AWS/ARGs should be considered only in the absence of properly functioning AWS/ARGs of IMD or the State Government, so when a working IMD station is available the private one should not be preferred.
questions.evidence: These must be optimally operational and be able to provide real time weather data. AWS/ARG of private agencies should only be considered in absence of properly functioning AWS/ARGs of IMD/ State Govt.

questions.q: In the sample weather insurance term sheet for dry spells (July to August phase), if our area had 16 dry days in a row, how much payout per hectare would that give?

Generally Yeshasvini is a Karnataka government health scheme for cooperative society members; enrolment is done through the member's cooperative society during the enrolment window, with an annual contribution that varies by year and category, so ask the society or the Cooperation Department for the current rate.

questions.q: After selling my paddy I have 50,000 rupees. If I put it in Kisan Vikas Patra at the post office, in how many months will it double?
questions.reference: Not covered in the documents. Generally Kisan Vikas Patra is a post office small-savings certificate that doubles the money over a fixed period set by the government's current interest rate; check the latest period at the post office.

questions.q: My tomato leaves are curling upward and turning small and yellow, and there are tiny white flies under the leaves. What is this and how do I stop it?
questions.reference: Not covered in the documents. Generally this looks like tomato leaf curl virus spread by whiteflies: remove and destroy infected plants early, use yellow sticky traps, reflective or nylon-net nursery protection, resistant varieties, and consult the local agriculture/KVK officer for a recommended insecticide.

questions.q: Two of my cows have round hard lumps all over the skin and fever. What should I do, is there a vaccine?
questions.reference: Not covered in the documents. Generally this sounds like lumpy skin disease: isolate the sick animals, control flies and mosquitoes, call the government veterinary doctor at once, and vaccinate healthy animals (goat-pox vaccine is used) as advised by the veterinary department.

questions.q: how to grow oyster mushroom in my shed with paddy straw how many days till first harvest
questions.reference: Not covered in the documents. Generally oyster mushroom is grown on chopped, soaked and pasteurised paddy straw filled in bags with spawn, kept dark and humid; pinheads come in about 2-3 weeks and the first harvest usually about 3-4 weeks after spawning. KVKs give training.

questions.q: For transplanted ragi, how much seed do I need per acre for the nursery and what spacing should I keep in the main field?
questions.reference: Not covered in the documents. Generally transplanted finger millet needs about 2 kg seed per acre for the nursery, with seedlings transplanted at about 3-4 weeks at roughly 22.5-30 cm between rows and 10-15 cm between plants; confirm with the local agriculture department's package of practices.

questions.q: ಮನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಗೋಬರ್ ಗ್ಯಾಸ್ ಘಟಕ ಹಾಕಬೇಕು. ಎರಡು ಹಸು ಇವೆ, ದಿನಕ್ಕೆ ಎಷ್ಟು ಸಗಣಿ ಬೇಕು ಮತ್ತು ಎಷ್ಟು ಗಾತ್ರದ ಘಟಕ ಸಾಕು?
questions.reference: Not covered in the documents. Generally a small family biogas plant of about 2 cubic metres needs roughly 40-50 kg of fresh dung a day mixed with an equal amount of water; 2 cows may give less, so size the plant to the dung available and check subsidy with the local rural development or KVK office.

questions.q: ರೇಷ್ಮೆ ಹುಳು ಸಾಕಣೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಉಜಿ ನೊಣದಿಂದ ಹುಳುಗಳು ಸಾಯುತ್ತಿವೆ. ಇದನ್ನು ತಡೆಯಲು ಏನು ಮಾಡಬೇಕು?
questions.reference: Not covered in the documents. Generally uzi fly is controlled by fixing wire-mesh on doors and windows of the rearing house, keeping it clean, destroying affected worms, and using parasitoids (like Nesolynx) or methods advised by the sericulture department.

questions.q: We keep bee boxes near our sunflower field. How many boxes per acre should I place to get better seed setting?
questions.reference: Not covered in the documents. Generally around 2-5 honeybee colonies per acre (about 5 per hectare) are suggested for sunflower pollination, placed at flowering; ask the horticulture department or KVK for local advice.

questions.q: Last year my onions rotted in the store within two months. How should I dry and store them so they last longer?
questions.reference: Not covered in the documents. Generally cure onions in the field or shade for about 1-2 weeks until necks are dry, remove damaged bulbs, and store in a well-ventilated, raised, cool and dry structure in thin layers; avoid moisture and stacking in heaps.

questions.q: kya Karnataka sarkar is saal kisano ka fasal karz maaf kar rahi hai? mera PACS me 80 hazar ka loan hai
questions.reference: Not covered in the documents. Generally loan waivers are announced by the State Government from time to time with their own rules; check the latest government order with your PACS or the Cooperation Department instead of relying on rumours, and keep repaying to stay eligible for fresh loans and interest benefits.

questions.q: I am a 35 year old farmer. If I join Atal Pension Yojana, how much do I have to pay every month to get 5,000 pension after 60?
questions.reference: Not covered in the documents. Generally Atal Pension Yojana is for people aged 18-40; the monthly contribution depends on the joining age and chosen pension (Rs 1,000-5,000). At 35 the contribution for Rs 5,000 pension is a few hundred rupees a month; check the exact chart at your bank or post office.

questions.q: धानको पराल जलाउनुको सट्टा कम्पोस्ट कसरी बनाउने? कति दिनमा तयार हुन्छ?
questions.reference: Not covered in the documents. Generally chop the straw, layer it with cow dung and soil, keep it moist and turn it every few weeks (a decomposer culture speeds it up); compost is usually ready in about 2-3 months. Burning straw harms soil and air.

questions.q: मेरो बाख्राहरूलाई जुकाको औषधि कति कति महिनामा खुवाउनुपर्छ?
questions.reference: Not covered in the documents. Generally goats are dewormed about every 3-4 months, especially before and after the rainy season, rotating medicines as advised by the government veterinary doctor; test dung samples if possible.

questions.q: In summer how many litres of water does one crossbred dairy cow need per day?
questions.reference: Not covered in the documents. Generally a milking crossbred cow needs roughly 60-100 litres of clean water a day in hot weather (more when giving more milk); give free access to water and shade.

questions.q: नीम कोटेड यूरिया और सामान्य यूरिया में क्या फर्क है? क्या इससे खाद कम लगती है?
questions.reference: Not covered in the documents. Generally neem-coated urea releases nitrogen more slowly, reduces losses and misuse, so plants use it more efficiently; use it as per soil test recommendations.

questions.q: ಅಡಿಕೆ ತೋಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಮಳೆಗಾಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಕಾಯಿ ಉದುರುತ್ತಿದೆ, ಕೊಳೆ ರೋಗ ಅಂತ ಹೇಳ್ತಾರೆ. ಏನು ಸಿಂಪಡಿಸಬೇಕು?
questions.reference: Not covered in the documents. Generally arecanut koleroga (fruit rot) is managed by spraying 1% Bordeaux mixture before the monsoon and again after about 40-45 days, and removing fallen infected nuts; consult the horticulture department or KVK.

questions.q: How do I work out how much urea, DAP and potash to put per acre for my maize without guessing?
questions.reference: Not covered in the documents. Generally base fertiliser doses on a soil test and the state's recommendation for maize, then convert the N-P-K amounts into urea, DAP and potash quantities; the local agriculture officer or KVK can calculate it for your field.

questions.q: How do I get a new electricity connection for the borewell pump on my farm in Karnataka and what documents are needed?
questions.reference: Not covered in the documents. Generally apply to your local electricity supply company (ESCOM) office for an irrigation pump set connection with land records, ID, borewell details and a licensed electrician's test report; ask the ESCOM for current rules and charges.

questions.q: मेरी गेहूं की फसल में दीमक लग गई है, जड़ें खोखली हो रही हैं। क्या करूं?
questions.reference: Not covered in the documents. Generally for termites use well-decomposed manure only, destroy termite mounds nearby, irrigate adequately, and use a recommended seed/soil treatment as advised by the local agriculture officer or KVK.
